Sarah — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support a multi-year structure and the reallocation you describe sounds reasonable. Quick confirmations and open questions so we can draft a clean private-offer term sheet: 

1) Reallocation: we can allow a 20% roll between years after the close of year 1, subject to no change in the committed aggregate. We'll reflect that as a one-time reallocation window in the term sheet.
2) True-up: 30-day true-up window is standard; we'll include a pro-rated credit for unused prepay if they terminate per the offer.
3) Overage cap: we can offer a stepped overage cap — 150% effective rate for up to 30% overage in a year, and then market rate beyond that. Do they want a hard cap on dollars?
4) Marketplace fees: we can offset up to 50% of the marketplace listing fee as a year-1 credit on the invoice (subject to AWS approval for private-offer pass-through). That will likely require coordination with AWS Marketplace contact.

I'll loop in our pricing and marketplace leads internally and send a draft term sheet and a sample year-by-year credit allocation matrix.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Market Sales (US)

Marissa / Diego — quick note from the marketplace side:

- AWS private offers allow promotions/credits but there are two modes: Marketplace-managed discounts (visible in the offer) and Seller-provided credits (handled off-invoice). For the 50% marketplace fee offset, we should first try the Marketplace-managed promo; AWS rep cc'd can confirm. If they push back, use Seller credit and capture it in the offer as a note.
- On invoicing mechanics, AWS will want the commitment and price visible; the reallocation language is allowed but needs to be explicit in the offer notes.
- DocuSign: if BlueNorth is OK, we can put the term sheet into DocuSign and have the marketplace link to the private-offer ID once signed.

I'll await Marissa's draft. Karthik

Sarah — thanks for your patience. Attached is a draft term sheet and a sample commitment schedule (see attachments: private_offer_term_sheet.pdf, commitment_schedule.xlsx). Summary of the negotiated mechanics we propose to include in the private offer:

- Term: 2-year annual prepay; total committed USD amount split by fiscal year (BlueNorth fiscal calendar).
- Discounts: 26% off list for 2-year prepay (illustrated in the attached table).
- Reallocation: single reallocation window after year 1 allowing up to 20% of year-1 credits to be moved to year 2; no retroactive moves back to year 1.
- True-up: 30-day true-up window following the close of each fiscal year with pro-rated credits for underutilization.
- Overage: excess consumption up to 30% billed at 150% effective rate for the excess tranche; consumption beyond that billed at the standard overage rate in the term sheet.
- Marketplace fee offset: Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 50% of the AWS Marketplace listing fee to the first paid invoice. This will be conveyed in the private-offer notes; AWS Marketplace is cc'd to confirm process.

Next steps: please review attachments and confirm if BlueNorth is comfortable with the proposed reallocation mechanics and overage cap wording. If confirmed, we'll convert the term sheet into DocuSign and initiate the private-offer workflow with AWS.

Thanks,
